explanation: Currents including the Gulf Stream swirl around it, trapping mats of floating sargassum seaweed, and European and American eels are thought to spawn there.

claims.text: The Sargasso Sea has no coastline and is bounded by ocean currents.
The Caribbean Sea, the Labrador Sea and the Norwegian Sea all have coastlines.
Ocean currents including the Gulf Stream circle the Sargasso Sea.
The Sargasso Sea holds floating mats of sargassum seaweed.
European and American eels are thought to spawn in the Sargasso Sea.

evidence.restatement: The Sargasso Sea is the one sea defined by currents rather than coasts.
The Caribbean, Labrador and Norwegian seas all border land.
The Gulf Stream, North Atlantic, Canary and North Equatorial currents ring the Sargasso Sea.
Floating sargassum seaweed gives the sea its name.
European and American eels are believed to spawn in the Sargasso Sea.
The Sargasso Sea is defined by ocean currents, not land: it is usually called the only sea without a land boundary.

claimResults.note: Bermuda lies inside it, so 'no coastline' is loose; 'no land boundary' is the exact form.
